purpose: Resolve the confounding of nominal zero output and the first DataPoints table knot in the existing 21-point evidence; test power reporting and source-phase composition separately.

baseline_comparisons.ordinary_reproduction: Original-triangle ordinary nominal 0 dBm: compare DCP and raw power and measured phase to prior interpolation-boundary ordinary target 0.
baseline_comparisons.sweep_to_ordinary: Shared nominal outputs -5, 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 dBm compare new amplitude sweep with prior interpolation-boundary ordinary observations; this is a cross-mode control.
baseline_comparisons.sweep_to_sweep: Shared nominal outputs 0, 10, 20 dBm compare new amplitude sweep with the historical natural-cubic-followup Compression Curve quick sweep; same path but different sweep mode, not reproduction of a full sweep.

hypotheses: Natural cubic spline on output dBm, numeric phase values, constant endpoint extension, added to measured source phase.

As above with bypass at the registered nominal zero-dBm output, independent of table knot location. This is a finite discrimination rule, not a proposed numerical implementation of a vendor condition.
As above with bypass at a registered nominal output coinciding with the first table knot, independent of absolute power.
scoring_axes: Actual DCP output W for each registered sweep point.
Ordinary DCP output W and independently verified raw carrier V/Z/P output W, scored separately.
Nominal-grid predictions diagnose the exceptional location only; they do not replace measured power axes or earlier evidence.
rules: No fitting, tolerance changes, deletion of zero points or overwriting prior evidence.
Original triangle is the first capture and a fresh reproduction control. Compare its ordinary zero point and shared sweep points with earlier observations before any other profile.
Ordinary and sweep phases always use their measured input node phase. Sweep input phase must be zero within 1e-10 radians, regardless of the schematic Source Phase parameter.
Prepare independent workspaces by replacing only exact XML text byte spans. Validate table SI arrays, all registered scalar parameters, workspace identity and source byte hashes before RunAnalysis.

Each profile must return all exact planned input-grid points. One extra final step is anticipated from the prior acquisition and must be retained in a separate extra-point collection; any other shape stops the workflow.
Run one capture at a time. A failed helper or post-capture validation blocks the next profile; no shell batch may continue after a nonzero result.
Stop on any diagnostic, timeout, unexpected workspace or parameter mismatch. One reserved call may be used only after a documented specific setup repair; do not rerun numerical disagreements.

Capture full timestamps, parameter readbacks, input/output node phase/power and raw carrier voltage/impedance. Quantized DCP versus raw power disagreement is a retained observation, not a reason to replace the registered scoring axis.

Save outputs to unique new files, close only dedicated copies, restore the pristine baseline without analysis, verify original parameter expressions and values, and leave the user-owned SystemVue process running.
This study does not by itself authorize a vendor-compatible DataPoints kernel, identify arbitrary-table interpolation uniquely, or prove multi-tone or Compression Curve behavior.
